document.title: Ambassador Dean's Cable. Subject: Gandhi/Ryzhkov Meeting: Discussion of Afghanistan
document.authors: Ambassador John Gunther Dean, U.S. Embassy New Delhi
document.publisher: National Security Archive (GWU), A New Phase in the Great Game: U.S., Soviets, India, Pakistan vied to shape a new Afghanistan in late 1980s | National Security Archive
document.note: Dean reports a two-hour talk with Rohen Sen on the Gandhi-Ryzhkov discussion of Afghanistan. Soviets and Indians shared a preference for a non-aligned Afghanistan and for keeping fundamentalists from power. Ryzhkov said the Soviets were in touch with all resistance groups and welcomed a larger Indian role.

persons.name: John Gunther Dean
persons.role: US Ambassador to India, author of cable

mentions.quote: ON THURSDAY, NOVEMBER 26, I HAD A TWO-HOUR CONVERSATION WITH GANDHI'S DIPLOMATIC ADVISOR RONEN SEN.

persons.name: Ronen Sen
persons.role: Diplomatic advisor to Indian Prime Minister Rajiv Gandhi

mentions.quote: GANDHI'S DIPLOMATIC ADVISOR RONEN SEN. THE MEETING WAS AT HIS REQUEST
INDIA BELIEVES THAT ANY COALITION OR INTERIM GOVERNMENT WHICH MIGHT EMERGE IN AFGHANISTAN SHOULD NOT BE DOMINATED BY FUNDAMENTALISTS.

persons.name: Nikolai Ryzhkov
persons.role: Soviet Prime Minister (Chairman of Council of Ministers) visiting India

mentions.quote: THE SOVIET PRIME MINISTER SAID THAT MOSCOW WAS "IN CLOSE CONTACT WITH IRAN ON AFGHANISTAN."
SOVIETS ARE KEEN ON PULLING OUT OF AFGHANISTAN AS GORBACHEV HAD TOLD GANDHI DIRECTLY.

persons.name: Najibullah
persons.role: Leader of Afghan PDPA government in Kabul

mentions.quote: THE SOVIETS ALSO TRIED TO CONVEY THE IMPRESSION OF NAJIB BEING A VERY DIFFERENT PERSON FROM HIS PREDECESSOR KARMAL.
CONTACT ALL GROUPS WITH A VIEW TO ENDING THE CONFLICT, SOMETHING KARMAL REFUSED TO DO.

persons.name: Mohammed Zahir Shah
persons.role: Exiled former King of Afghanistan, possible role in settlement

mentions.quote: SOME OF THE FUNDAMENTALIST GROUPS IN PESHAWAR REMAIN OPPOSED TO A SIGNIFICANT ROLE FOR THE KING.

sources_cited: STATE 361795 (US message to Gandhi on Afghanistan)
key_claims: India and the USSR shared an objective of preventing a fundamentalist-dominated Afghan interim government.
Gandhi warned that fundamentalist victory in Afghanistan would affect Soviet Central Asia and aggravate India-Pakistan tensions over Kashmir.
Ryzhkov tied Soviet troop withdrawal timing to assurances/guarantees of non-interference.
The Soviets claimed contact with all resistance groups and thought field commanders were more amenable to settlement than Peshawar groups.
Ryzhkov presented Najibullah as more pragmatic than Karmal, open to Islam and coalition government.
India assessed the PDPA as narrowly based and unable to survive in a PDPA-controlled interim government.
Dean saw the detailed Indian readout as evidence of close US-India relations.
